pergunta: Without Monte Carlo over the error, what is the value of the design term of the bias Corollary (cor:bias, main.tex l.272): Sum_i p_i e_i / Sum_i p_i - mu_U, for the constant and the calibrated FSPL (b), in the populations 'todos' (all nodes) and 'validos' (valid nodes), in the four Q1 cells?

parametros.p_i: (k_te/N) * p_{i|te}; p_{i|te} in [lo(m), hi(m)] (prop:inclusion (ii)); exact = lo(m) where the reading declares it
parametros.e_i: calibrated ONCE on split seed=42 (constant=median RSSI of training; FSPL(b) offset by the median of the valid training nodes), as in 2.3
parametros.extremos_intervalo: exact extremes of the ratio with p in a box (Dinkelbach)

leituras.L_no_a_no: exact (=lo) where m=0 or condition (iii) holds at the node; other nodes bounds only (primary, fixed a priori)
leituras.T_classe: exact at m=0,1,3; bounds only at m=2 and m>=4 (main.tex l.312)
leituras.C_todas: lo treated as exact in every class m (point)
leituras.U_so_m0: exact only at m=0; m>=1 bounds only

desvios_do_criterio: The decision criterion compares the design term with 'the difference (b)-(a) of fase2/2.3', which is the TOTAL bias (design + ratio). Reported as vs_b_menos_mu_2_3_MC (comparator of the criterion, SE = sd/sqrt(n_A)); also reported is the comparator WITHOUT the ratio term: (c)-(a) of 2.3 reconstructed (frequency over 100 split draws; bootstrap SE over the 100 split draws) and the frequency over 200 split draws of this script.

The seeds/split draws of 2.3 (100, RandomState(20260927)) differ from the 200 of 1.8 (RandomState(20260926)); the four cells share the same grid of 132 blocks and the same seeds (they are not independent MC replicates).
mu_U uses e_i recalculated at full precision (checked against 'a' of 2.3 to 1.5e-3 dB); 'a' of 2.3 is rounded to 3 decimal places.
